title: EXPLORE MEMBERSHIP OR COMMUNITY WITH CHATGPT
content:
A membership or community subscription works when continued belonging, access, participation, resources, accountability, or interaction provides ongoing value.

A group existing behind a paywall is not automatically a membership people will keep paying for. Define what members continue receiving or experiencing.

COMMUNITY CAN BE PART OF THE VALUE, NOT ALL OF IT
Some memberships are valuable because members help one another. Others center on expert access, events, resources, accountability, networking, or a shared activity. Often the strongest concept combines several elements around a specific member need.

THE EMPTY-ROOM PROBLEM
If the concept depends heavily on member-to-member interaction, ask what the first members receive before the community is large. A membership should have a useful starting experience rather than requiring scale before it becomes worthwhile.

MODERATION AND PRESENCE ARE WORK
Communities may require welcoming members, moderation, scheduling, conflict management, support, events, and ongoing participation. Decide how much of that role you want.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

Interview me about a membership or community subscription. Ask who the members are, what they have in common, what ongoing outcome or experience they want, what they would receive immediately, what improves through participation over time, whether member-to-member interaction matters, and how much moderation, facilitation, content, events, or personal access I want to provide.

Test the empty-room version: explain what the first ten members would get even before a large community exists. Help me distinguish benefits that scale from benefits that require my direct time.

Identify assumptions about demand, platform needs, moderation, safety, privacy, content rights, workload, and pricing that require research.

At the end give me:
- Intended member
- Ongoing need/outcome
- Core membership benefits
- Value available from day one
- Role of member interaction
- My ongoing responsibilities
- Main assumptions to verify
- Concise business-direction statement

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If clear, continue to PDF 46. If customers mainly need continuing access to your personal expertise or help, compare PDF 36.
